Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.example>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Promptset-X A/B delta — proposed acceptance thresholds

Team —

We finished the cross-region A/B run for promptset-X against production v1.3. High-level: the new promptset increases helpfulness in free-form tasks but we’re seeing a ~1.9% absolute drop on instruction-following for our curated safety-sensitive prompts (see attached eval-results-q1.csv). That failure mode shows up as omissions or hallucinated steps in 7 of the 50 sampled cases (screenshot-sample-failures.png).

Questions for product + infra:
- What acceptance threshold do we want to gate on for instruction-following (absolute delta vs relative)?
- If we breach, do we rollback immediately or do a staged rollback/canary with metric gating?
- Who owns customer-facing comms if we need a partial rollback for Acme (they're in the middle of a pilot)?

Attached: eval-results-q1.csv (summary + per-case tags), screenshot-sample-failures.png. I sketched a suggested matrix in proposed-acceptance-matrix.xlsx — quick summary in the sheet 'recap'.

Short ask: Can product/ops propose concrete numeric thresholds and immediate mitigations by EOD tomorrow so we can present to CS for Acme?

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Promptset-X A/B delta — proposed acceptance thresholds

Thanks Marissa — good catch and clear summary. A couple of framing notes before we land thresholds:

- The pilot with Acme is low-volume but they use instruction-following heavily; a visible regression there has outsized customer impact.
- We need thresholds that map cleanly to runbook actions (e.g., immediate rollback, canary hold, or proceed with monitoring).

Dev + Jonas — can you two propose the metric definitions and exact numeric gates? Suggest we separate: 1) safety-sensitive instruction-following (hard gate) and 2) general helpfulness/fluency (soft gate).

Suggested initial policy (for discussion):
- Hard gate (safety-sensitive instruction-following): absolute delta > 1.0% => pause rollout and rollback to v1.3 unless mitigations reduce delta below 0.5% within 2 hours.
- Soft gate (helpfulness): relative improvement allowed; if helpfulness drops but <2% absolute and non-safety, continue with closer monitoring.

Marissa — please flag any cases in the CSV that are clearly safety-critical so we can prioritize.

I'll pull legal/CS in if rollback impacts pilot timelines; we should aim to have a customer note drafted if we need to throttle.

-Steph
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Promptset-X A/B delta — proposed acceptance thresholds

Quick technical notes on measurement and mitigation options:

1) Measurement windows: the 1.9% number looks like an aggregate across regions and user segments; we should compute per-region and per-session-type deltas (pilot vs non-pilot) — some of the signal is concentrated in mobile sessions.

2) Attribution: a handful of fails are prompt-engineering regressions (prompt truncation on long context). Short-term mitigation: enable prefix-preservation for the promptset variant (config flag) which we can toggle without model re-deploy; it reduced similar failures in last week's smaller run.

3) Canary plan options (ops):
- Immediate hard rollback: revert routing for all Acme traffic to v1.3 (fast, customer-safe).
- Staged canary: restrict new promptset to 10% of traffic with metric gates every 30 minutes and auto-fallback on the hard gate.
- Config toggle: enable prefix-preservation for the variant and re-run a 500-sample check (fast, low-risk).

I can run the 500-sample recheck + per-region breakdown in ~3 hours if we get sign-off. I recommend try toggle -> recheck -> if still high, do staged canary -> if fails, rollback. That avoids immediate broad rollback and gives CS time to prep.

-Dev
Dev Patel
Engineering Manager, Runtime

Subject: Re: Promptset-X A/B delta — proposed acceptance thresholds

Adding ML perspective and concrete acceptance numbers from our eval deck:

- Measurement: use weighted absolute delta on the instruction-following score (weighted by severity tag: safety-critical=3, medium=2, low=1). We evaluated tradeoffs and recommend the following:
  * Hard rollback threshold: weighted-absolute-delta >= 1.25 => immediate rollback.
  * Remediation window: 0.6 <= delta < 1.25 => enable mitigations (prefix-preservation) + 2-hour re-eval; if no improvement, rollback.
  * Soft threshold: delta < 0.6 => proceed but increase sampling for next 48h.

- Canary ramp: if remediation window is triggered, use 10%->30%->60% steps (2-hour windows) with auto-fallback on the hard gate.

- Customer impact: for Acme pilot, given their profile I recommend we apply immediate reroute to v1.3 for their Org ID while we run the remediation path for public rollout. That minimizes customer churn while allowing us to continue the broader rollout with controls.

I attached the short calculation sheet to the proposed matrix (see 'calc' tab). Happy to sync 30m today to align.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Applied ML, Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — this is actionable. Summary & next steps:

1) Immediate: Dev to enable prefix-preservation on the promptset variant and run a 500-sample recheck (Dev ETA: 3h). Jonas will compute the weighted-delta and report back.
2) Customer protection: CS will reroute Acme org to v1.3 now (Lauren, please confirm once done).
3) Gate matrix we agreed to (finalized):
   - weighted-absolute-delta >= 1.25 => rollback to v1.3 for public traffic; immediate reroute for pilots affected.
   - 0.6 <= delta < 1.25 => remediation window (toggle + 2h re-eval) then rollback if no improvement.
   - delta < 0.6 => continue rollout with doubled sampling for 48h.
4) Documentation & comms: Lauren to draft customer note for Acme once reroute completes; Legal on standby for formal wording if pilot SLA is affected.
5) Owner assignments: Dev (mitigation + recheck), Jonas (metric calc + final pass), Marissa (case triage + sample annotations), Lauren (CS comms + reroute), Steph (exec escalation if rollback).

Please update INF-4821 with outcomes & paste final calc sheet. If any objections, flag within 2 hours; otherwise we proceed.

-Stephanie
